title: Four signatures of the workspace band
takeaway: Four statistics derived from the J-lens, each plotted against layer depth, change sharply at the same two places: around a third of the way through the model (~L38) and shortly before the output (~L92). The paper reads these two inflections as the start and end of the workspace band — with the caveat that all four metrics come from the J-lens itself, so an early-layer blind spot of the lens cannot be ruled out.
walkthrough:
This figure gives quantitative backing to the three-band picture of [[layer-bands]] — sensory, workspace, motor. It holds four panels, (a) through (d). Each panel plots one statistic of the [[jacobian-lens]] against layer depth. Layers follow the paper's convention of [[layer-percentage-indexing]]: 25 evenly spaced layers of Claude Sonnet 4.5's [[residual-stream]], relabeled 0 to 100, so a layer number reads as a percentage of depth. Together the four curves are the paper's [[workspace-boundary-metrics]].

Panel (a) plots [[lens-next-token-accuracy]]: the fraction of positions at which any of the lens's top-$k$ tokens matches the model's own top-1 next-token prediction. The curve sits near zero through the early layers. It ticks up at the workspace start, rises slowly through the middle, and jumps steeply in the last few layers. The paper reads the late jump as the end of the workspace: from there on, lens vectors act as [[motor-layers]] content driving the imminent output, not as intermediate results available for further processing.

Panel (b) plots the [[readout-excess-kurtosis]] of the lens's logit distribution at a single position and layer, averaged over many activations. High [[kurtosis]] means the readout is sharply peaked on a few tokens rather than spread randomly. The curve is near zero through the first third of the depth, rises from about a third of the way in, and falls in the last few layers. The early rise marks the workspace onset: before it, the [[j-space]] carries essentially no meaningful content.

Panel (c) plots [[top1-autocorrelation]]: how often the same token stays at the top of the readout from position $t$ to position $t+\Delta$, shown as $\Delta$ log probability over a position-shuffled null. Persistence signals abstract content that survives across the token stream; its absence signals token-local content. The curve hugs the null early, rises at the same layer as the other metrics, peaks across the middle band, and falls back late.

Panel (d) plots the [[j-space-effective-dimensionality]]: the fraction of residual-stream dimensions needed to capture a given share of variance across the lens vectors $W_U J_\ell$. It is small early — the lens collapses to a thin subspace — then rises sharply at the onset as the vectors fan out, and rises again, less dramatically, at the motor transition, where $J_\ell$ approaches the identity and the lens inherits the full dimensionality of the [[unembedding-matrix]].

All four curves inflect near L38 and L92. The paper flags one caveat: every metric here is lens-derived, so a workspace the J-lens cannot resolve in early layers would be invisible to this analysis.

terms.definition: The fraction of text positions at which any of the J-lens's top-k tokens equals the model's actual top-1 next-token prediction, plotted per layer. Near zero early, slowly rising through the workspace, and jumping steeply in the final layers.

Kurtosis of the J-lens readout's logit distribution at a single position and layer, in excess of a Gaussian, computed over a large set of activations. High values mean the readout concentrates on a few tokens instead of looking random.

The rate at which the same token remains at the top of the lens readout at position t and at position t+Δ, expressed as Δ log probability relative to a position-shuffled null. High values mean the J-space holds content that persists across the token stream.

The fraction of residual-stream dimensions needed to capture a given share of the variance across the layer's J-lens vectors. Small when the lens collapses to a thin subspace, large when the vectors span most of the residual stream.

The paper's readout technique: one vector per vocabulary token per layer, giving the direction that encodes the model's potential to verbalize that token. All four panels are statistics of its readouts or its vectors.

The layer-ℓ J-lens vectors as rows: the corpus-averaged Jacobian $J_\ell$ from layer ℓ to the final layer, composed with the unembedding matrix $W_U$. Panel (d) measures the variance structure of this set of vectors.
The corpus-averaged Jacobian matrix from layer ℓ's residual stream to the final layer. In the last layers it approaches the identity, which is why panel (d) rises again there.
The unembedding matrix, the model's final linear map from residual stream to vocabulary scores. Its full dimensionality is what the lens inherits in the motor layers.
The shared horizontal axis of all four panels: 25 evenly sampled layers of the residual stream, reindexed to 0–100 so that a layer number reads as a percentage of the model's depth.

Rank cutoffs on the lens readout's token ranking. Panel (a) asks whether the model's top-1 prediction appears anywhere in the lens's top k tokens; panel (c) tracks only the single highest-ranked lens token.
Panel (c)'s vertical unit: the log-probability of the top-1 token repeating across a position gap, minus the same quantity under the shuffled null, so zero means no more persistence than chance.
The baseline for panel (c): the repeat rate expected if lens readouts were assigned to positions at random, removing any genuine across-position persistence.

The two depth landmarks the figure locates: the onset near L38, where kurtosis, autocorrelation, and dimensionality all rise, and the offset near L92, where accuracy jumps, kurtosis and autocorrelation fall, and lens content turns motor.
The paper's term for late-layer lens content tied to the imminent output token rather than to intermediate computation; the final steep rise in panel (a) is read as the switch to this regime.

numbers.meaning: Sub-panels (a)–(d), one per boundary metric: next-token accuracy, excess kurtosis, top-1 autocorrelation, and effective dimensionality. Their agreement, not any one curve, is the figure's argument.

The workspace onset: about 38% of the way through the model's depth, where excess kurtosis, autocorrelation, and effective dimensionality all rise sharply. Before this layer the J-space carries essentially no meaningful content.

The workspace offset: about 92% of depth, shortly before the output, where next-token accuracy jumps steeply and kurtosis and autocorrelation fall back — the switch from intermediate to motor content.
The layer axis range: 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers reindexed so layer numbers read as percentages of depth, making bands comparable across models of different depths.
The number of evenly spaced layers actually sampled; the paper notes that this subsampling exaggerates how sharp the band transitions look.
The fraction of early depth over which panels (a)–(c) stay near zero or near the null — the sensory band, where the J-space is effectively empty.
The early-layer baseline of panels (a)–(c): readouts no more peaked, predictive, or persistent than chance, which is what an empty workspace looks like under these metrics.
